description: Epic Paused lifecycle state (reversible, non-terminal, link-preserving) with pause/resume API, list/detail UI, and Epic detail topbar number fix

tasks.title: Epic aggregate: add Paused status with Pause/Resume transitions and MarkDone guard
tasks.description: Extend the Epic domain aggregate (from #178) with a `Paused` value on `EpicStatus`, `Pause(reason)`/`Resume()` transition methods, a `PauseReason` field, a new `EpicPausedCannotMarkDoneException`, and an explicit Paused guard at the top of `MarkDone`. Pause/Resume emit only `EpicStatusChanged` (never `EpicClosed`, so the grain unbind side-effect cannot fire). Extend the `ToStatusName`/`StatusName`/`ParseStatus` maps with the paused branch. `EpicAlreadyTerminalException` and `EpicProgress.IsTerminal` stay unchanged so Paused is non-terminal.
acceptanceCriteria: `EpicStatus` has a `Paused` member and status name maps round-trip `paused`.
`Pause(reason)` from `active` sets status to `paused`, persists the reason, records one `EpicStatusChanged(active→paused)`, and does not remove linked issues.
`Pause` on an already-paused Epic is an idempotent no-op; `Pause`/`MarkDone`/`Close` from `done` or `closed` throw `EpicAlreadyTerminalException`.
`Resume()` from `paused` sets status back to `active` and clears the stored reason.
`MarkDone` on a `paused` Epic throws `EpicPausedCannotMarkDoneException` (the existing `EnsureNotTerminal` alone would not catch this).
`Close()` from `paused` is allowed (no resume required).
`EpicProgress.IsTerminal` returns false for `paused` (unchanged, verified by test).

Domain specs in EpicTransitionsSpecs/EpicLifecycleSpecs cover pause, resume, paused→done rejection, terminal guards, reason persist/clear, and link preservation; the existing Epic domain test suite still passes.
tasks.output: Epic aggregate models the Paused lifecycle with locked transitions and passing domain unit tests
tasks.notes: Files: packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Epic/Domain/EpicStatus.cs, Epic.Transitions.cs, Epic.cs (PauseReason backing field), EpicLifecycleExceptions.cs, EpicProgress.cs (no change, assert only), Events/EpicEvent.cs (no new event type). Mirror the existing trait-tagged spec style in tests/Mohist.Server.Tests/Specs/Epic/Domain/.

tasks.title: Epic API + persistence: pause/resume grain methods, PauseReason column, routes, and DTO wiring
tasks.description: Add `PauseAsync(string? reason)` and `ResumeAsync()` to `IEpicGrain`/`EpicGrain` reusing the existing load→mutate→MapToRow→ApplyPendingEvents→save flow; add a nullable `PauseReason` column to `EpicRow` plus an EF migration; add `PauseReason` to `EpicDto`, `EpicWithProgressDto`, and `EpicDetailDto` and thread it through `EpicQuerier` and the grain mappers; expose `POST /epics/:id/pause` (optional `{reason}` body) and `POST /epics/:id/resume`, and map `EpicPausedCannotMarkDoneException` to HTTP 409 `EPIC_PAUSED_CANNOT_MARK_DONE`.
acceptanceCriteria: A new EF migration adds a nullable `PauseReason` column and `db.Database.Migrate()` applies it cleanly on startup.
`POST /api/projects/{ref}/epics/:id/pause` with optional `{reason}` returns the Epic DTO with status `paused`, persists the reason, and does not unbind any linked issue.
`POST /api/projects/{ref}/epics/:id/resume` returns the Epic DTO with status `active` and clears the reason.
`POST .../epics/:id/done` on a paused Epic returns 409 with code `EPIC_PAUSED_CANNOT_MARK_DONE`; `.../close` from paused still succeeds.
`GET .../epics` and `GET .../epics/:id` responses include `pauseReason` (null when absent).
Pause/Resume routes accept either the raw Epic id or the Epic number path segment (parity with existing done/close routes).
API specs (tests/Mohist.Server.Tests/Specs/Epic/Api/EpicApiSpecs.cs) cover pause, resume, paused-done rejection, reason persistence/clearing, and no-unbind-on-pause.
tasks.output: Pause/resume are callable over the REST API with persisted reason and a nullable column; existing done/close paths unaffected
tasks.notes: Files: Epic/Grains/EpicGrain.cs (+ IEpicGrain), Epic/Services/EpicDtos.cs, EpicQuerier.cs, Infrastructure/Data/Epic/EpicRow.cs, Infrastructure/Data/Db/MohistDbContext.cs (entity config for PauseReason), Infrastructure/Data/Migrations/<new>, Api/EpicRoutes.cs. Follow the existing one-action-per-route pattern; do NOT overload SetStatusAsync.

tasks.title: Web: Epic list Paused group, amber status badge, and shared frontend types
tasks.description: Add `Paused = 'paused'` to the frontend `EpicStatus` enum and an optional `pauseReason` field to the Epic/EpicWithProgress/EpicDetail types; extend the `StatusBadge` color/label maps (list and detail) with an amber Paused branch; add a `Paused` section to `EpicListPage` ordered between `Active` and `Done`; visually de-emphasize paused cards so they do not compete with active work in the '推进' view.
acceptanceCriteria: `EpicStatus` enum and Epic/EpicWithProgress/EpicDetail types include `Paused` and `pauseReason`.
The `StatusBadge` renders an amber style for `paused` that is distinct from active (green), done (blue), and closed (grey).
The Epics list renders a `Paused` section only when paused Epics exist, positioned after `Active` and before `Done`.
Paused Epic cards are visually de-emphasized (e.g. reduced opacity/muted styling) relative to active cards.
EpicListPage tests assert the Paused section ordering and the paused badge rendering; the page renders without regressions when there are zero paused Epics.
tasks.output: Paused Epics appear as a distinct amber section in the Epic list, de-emphasized and correctly ordered
tasks.notes: Files: packages/web/src/entities/epic/model/types.ts (shared types land here first), pages/epics/ui/EpicListPage.tsx (StatusBadge + grouping), pages/epic-detail/ui/EpicDetailPage.tsx (its local StatusBadge map). Owns the shared frontend type changes that T-004 builds on.

tasks.title: Web: Epic detail Pause/Resume action with reason dialog and Mark-Done guard
tasks.description: Add `pauseEpic(id, reason?)`/`resumeEpic(id)` API clients and `usePauseEpic`/`useResumeEpic` react-query hooks (invalidating epic + detail query keys); render a `Pause` action on active Epics that opens a confirmation Dialog with an optional reason Input, and a `Resume` action on paused Epics; disable Mark Done while paused with a 'resume first' hint; display the persisted `pauseReason` near the status badge when present.
acceptanceCriteria: `pauseEpic`/`resumeEpic` clients call the new endpoints and the hooks invalidate `['epics']` and `['epics', projectId, id]` on success.
On an active Epic, the `Pause` action opens a confirm Dialog with an optional reason field; confirming transitions the Epic to `paused` and leaves linked issues unchanged.
On a paused Epic, the action becomes `Resume` and returns the Epic to `active`.
Mark Done is disabled while paused and shows a 'resume first' affordance (in addition to the existing `!readyToMarkDone` guard).
The persisted pause reason is displayed on the detail page when non-null.
EpicDetailPage tests cover Pause dialog + reason submission, Resume toggle, Mark-Done-disabled-while-paused, and reason display.
tasks.output: Users can pause/resume an Epic from the detail page with an optional persisted reason; Mark Done is correctly gated while paused
tasks.notes: Files: packages/web/src/entities/epic/api/client.ts (+ queries.ts for hooks), pages/epic-detail/ui/EpicDetailPage.tsx (action row at lines ~387-418, new Pause confirm Dialog mirroring the existing close-confirm Dialog). Reuses shared types from T-003.

tasks.title: Web: fix Epic detail topbar to show Epic #<number> instead of truncated raw id
tasks.description: Fix `usePageTitle()` in `widgets/app-shell/ui/Header.tsx` so that on `/epics/:id` it resolves the Epic's display number (reuse the existing `useEpic` hook) and renders `Epic #<number>` (e.g. `Epic #1`), with a loading fallback of `Epic #…`. Remove the raw-id `params.id?.slice(0, 8)` truncation on both the first-segment and section branches. Leave all other route title bindings untouched.
acceptanceCriteria: On an Epic detail page the topbar title shows `Epic #<number>` using the Epic's number, not a raw id prefix like `Epic #epic_313`.
The title resolves correctly whether the path segment is the raw Epic id or the Epic number (server resolves both).
While the number is loading, the title falls back gracefully (e.g. `Epic #…`) without layout shift.
Titles for the Epics list page, issue detail page, and other routes are unchanged.
A Header/page-title test asserts `Epic #<number>` rendering and that issue/other route titles are unaffected.
tasks.output: Epic detail topbar shows the human Epic number; other route titles unchanged
tasks.notes: Files: packages/web/src/widgets/app-shell/ui/Header.tsx (usePageTitle lines 18-21 and 32-33). Independent of the Paused work — reuses the existing useEpic hook and the number already present in EpicDetail; react-query dedupes against the detail page fetch.
